text.p: These are the leading stories in Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Socialist party government ministers blame their president Ljubisav Ivanov for despotism and disrespect of the legally elected party bodies. Health Minister Ilija Filipce and two ministers without portfolio Ljubo Trpovski and Vlado Naumovski publicly distance themselves from the contents of the letter addressed to the Social Democrats in which Ivanov attacks the government for corruption and total failure of Macedonia's economy.

- The Liberal and Democratic parties are to be united. The paper comments that "this means an expansion of the political centre in Macedonia". It quotes unofficial sources as saying that Petar Gosev, president of the Democratic Party, will head the combined party. Liberal party president Stojan Andov is considered a possible presidential candidate for 1999 elections.
- Education Minister Sofija Todorova state at the parliamentary commission for education that "Macedonia will not allow parallel educational systems".

- Foreign Minister Ljubomir Frckovski was on a one-day visit to Croatia to meet Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and Foreign Minister Mate Granich. Sources in the Macedonian foreign ministry stated that "this means continuity of the development of good relations between Macedonia and Croatia".
- Official statistics say the average salary in Macedonia in 1996 was 9015 denars, or about 320 deutsch marks. This is up 4.2 from 1995.
- Ten Albanian citizens have been expelled from Debar (western Macedonia) for crossing the border with false passports. They were expelled for one years.
